security_headers.name: Strict-Transport-Security
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Users can be downgraded to HTTP and become vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. Session cookies can be intercepted.
security_headers.fix: Add 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' to all HTTPS responses. Submit to HSTS preload list at hstspreload.org after testing.

security_headers.name: Content-Security-Policy
security_headers.recommended_value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none';
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks can execute arbitrary JavaScript in users' browsers. Data exfiltration and session hijacking risk.
security_headers.fix: Implement a Content-Security-Policy header. Start with 'default-src self' and progressively allow necessary sources. Use CSP nonces for inline scripts. Test with report-only mode first.

security_headers.name: X-Frame-Options
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Clickjacking attacks can embed your site in an iframe and trick users into performing unintended actions (e.g., unauthorized fund transfers, settings changes).
security_headers.fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'. Prefer using frame-ancestors in CSP for modern browsers. Both headers can coexist for backward compatibility.

security_headers.name: X-Content-Type-Options
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute files as different content types. An attacker-controlled image upload could be executed as JavaScript.
security_headers.fix: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to all responses. This is a simple, low-risk header with high security value.

security_headers.name: Referrer-Policy
security_headers.impact_if_missing: The full URL including query parameters (potentially containing sensitive data like tokens, session IDs) is sent in the Referer header to third-party sites.
security_headers.fix: Add 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' to limit referrer information sent cross-origin.

security_headers.name: Permissions-Policy
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Malicious scripts injected via XSS could access device APIs (camera, microphone, location) without user consent.
security_headers.fix: Add 'Permissions-Policy' header to explicitly disable browser features your application doesn't use.

security_headers.name: Cache-Control
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Sensitive data may be cached in browser history or shared caches, leaking information to subsequent users on shared computers.
security_headers.fix: Add 'Cache-Control: no-store' for pages containing sensitive data (dashboards, profile pages, admin panels).

security_headers.name: Server
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Exposes web server software and version, helping attackers identify known CVEs for your exact server version.
security_headers.fix: Remove or obfuscate the Server header. In nginx: 'server_tokens off;'. In Apache: 'ServerTokens Prod; ServerSignature Off;'.

security_headers.name: X-Powered-By
security_headers.impact_if_missing: Reveals application framework and version (e.g., 'PHP/8.1.0', 'Express'), aiding targeted attacks against known vulnerabilities.
security_headers.fix: Disable X-Powered-By in your framework config. In Express: 'app.disable("x-powered-by")'. In PHP: 'expose_php = Off' in php.ini.

security_headers.name: Access-Control-Allow-Origin
security_headers.impact_if_missing: CORS misconfiguration (wildcard *) allows any malicious website to make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of logged-in users.
security_headers.fix: Specify exact allowed origins. Never use '*' with credentials. Validate Origin against a whitelist. Return specific origins, not a wildcard.
